judgments.catchwords: 1. This Originating Summons concerns two parcels of land situated in Balik Pulau, Pulau Pinang, namely Lot 434 held under Geran Mukim No. GM 240 and Lot 435 held under Geran Mukim No. GM 241 (collectively, "the Lands"). 2. Both titles contain an endorsement under the heading Perkara Lain Yang Melibatkan Hakmilik, which reads: "Subject to Provisions of Land Conservation Act 1960". The Applicant contends that the endorsement has become obsolete following the repeal of the legislation which extended the Land Conservation Act 1960 to the State of Pulau Pinang. 3. The Applicant therefore seeks declarations that the Lands are no longer subject to the Land Conservation Act 1960 and orders directing the Respondents to take the necessary steps to cancel the endorsement from the respective titles and the State Land Register. 4. The First Respondent does not dispute that the legislation extending the Land Conservation Act 1960 to the State of Pulau Pinang has been repealed. However, the Respondents maintain that the repeal did not automatically cancel the endorsement appearing on the titles. Their objection is principally that the endorsement can only be removed upon completion of the prescribed administrative procedure. 5. Having considered the affidavits and the written submissions filed by the parties, this Court allowed the application, subject to the directions set out at the conclusion of these Grounds.

judgments.title: AMINUL ISLAM BIN ABDUL NOR v CHIN BOON LONG
judgments.catchwords: Catchwords: This is an appeal on my ruling dated 9 September 2026 to transfer the Plaintiff’s suit from the High Court to the Session’s Court following this Court’s motion under Order 57 rule 1A of the Rules of Court 2012 – the transfer was carried out pursuant to the Court’s exercise of its discretion suo motu under Order 57 rule 1A of ROC 2012 – there were 8 Impugned Defamatory Statements – this is a case of defamation where Defendant have published statements which are allegedly defamatory to the Plaintiff – the merits or otherwise of both party’s claims and counterclaims have not been adjudicated in Court – it must be emphasized that before a Court can transfer the proceedings to Session Court on its own motion under O57 r1A ROC 2012 satisfied that doing so is just an appropriate – this determination should be made in the interest of the parties involved while taking into accounts both the subject matter and overall value of the claim – damages including (i) General damages for defamation in the sum of RM100,000,000.00; (ii) Aggravated damages (iii) Exemplary damages – the general damages were quantified which is against Order 18 rule 12 1A of the ROC 2012 – as set out above, the quantum of the claims for reliefs sought by the Plaintiff exceeded RM1,000,000.00 – given that the dispute involves alleged defamation, the Court can take judicial note that, should liability be established, the quantum of damages typically awarded in such cases would not exceed RM1,000,000.00 – this is an appeal on my ruling and not my decision nor judgment as defined under section 3 of the Courts of Judicature Act – it is trite the High Court is bound by the principle of stare decisis, the damages to be awarded, if parties succeed, will not exceed RM1,000,000.00 – even though the Court possesses the requisite jurisdiction to hear the proceedings, the issue is whether it is more suitable to transfer the proceedings to the Session Court – After all, a Session Court is vested with jurisdiction when the amount in dispute or value of the subject matter does not exceed RM1,000,000.00 as prescribed by Section 65 of the Subordinate Courts Act – it is evident that an experienced counsel in a defamation suit would anticipate that should they succeed, the damages awarded by the Court are unlikely to exceed the jurisdictional limit of the Sessions Court – it is in the interest of the parties to proceed there for time efficiency and cost-effectiveness – furthermore, the parties’ interest will not be prejudiced as they retain the right of appeal to the High Court – I ordered the present suit to be transferred to the Sessions Court with no order as to costs.
